68981-through-a-pocket-lens.title: A Pocket Lens
68981-through-a-pocket-lens.creator: Unknown
68981-through-a-pocket-lens.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The object of this little book is to show how much may be seen with an ordinary pocket lens, and with a simple microscope; and, as far as possible, to dispel the idea, far too common, especially among beginners, that no real work can be done unless one has a compound microscope, with a large battery of lenses and an array of ‘accessories.’

arxiv-2112-12036.title: Tracial oscillation zero and 𝒵 {\cal Z} -stability
arxiv-2112-12036.creator: Huaxin Lin
arxiv-2112-12036.description: Abstract Let A A be a (not necessarily unital) separable non-elementary simple amenable C ∗ C^{*} -algebra whose tracial basis may not have finite covering dimension and may not be compact but satisfies a certain condition (C). We show that A A is 𝒵 {\cal Z} -stable if and only if A A has strict comparison for positive elements.

arxiv-2203-03039.title: Landau–Ginzburg mirror, quantum differential equations and qKZ difference equations for a partial flag variety
arxiv-2203-03039.creator: Vitaly Tarasov ∘ \mskip 2.00002mu{}^{\circ} and Alexander Varchenko ⋆ \mskip 2.00002mu{}^{\star}
arxiv-2203-03039.description: Abstract . We consider the system of quantum differential equations for a partial flag variety and construct a basis of solutions in the form of multidimensional hypergeometric functions, that is, we construct a Landau–Ginzburg mirror for that partial flag variety. In our construction, the solutions are labeled by elements of the K \mskip 2.00002muK\mskip-2.

arxiv-2212-12123.creator: Manik Dhar, Sivakanth Gopi
arxiv-2212-12123.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Manik Dhar, Sivakanth Gopi. arxiv-2303-11990.title: Blow-ups and normal bundles in connective and nonconnective derived geometries Thanks: The second author was supported by the Göran Gustafsson foundation. The paper is a result of a research visit partially supported by the CMSC of the University of Haifa and the Signeul foundation.
arxiv-2303-11990.creator: Oren Ben-Bassat, Jeroen Hekking
arxiv-2303-11990.description: Abstract . This work presents a generalization of derived blow-ups and of the derived deformation to the normal bundle from derived algebraic geometry to any geometric context. The latter is our proposed globalization of a derived algebraic context, itself a generalization of the theory of simplicial commutative rings.

arxiv-2305-18393.title: Training Private Models That Know What They Don’t Know
arxiv-2305-18393.creator: Stephan Rabanser, Anvith Thudi, Abhradeep Thakurta, Krishnamurthy (Dj) Dvijotham, Nicolas Papernot
arxiv-2305-18393.description: Abstract Training reliable deep learning models which avoid making overconfident but incorrect predictions is a longstanding challenge. This challenge is further exacerbated when learning has to be differentially private: protection provided to sensitive data comes at the price of injecting additional randomness into the learning process.

arxiv-2307-12469.title: How Effective Are They? Exploring Large Language Model Based Fuzz Driver Generation CCS: Security and privacy Software security engineering
arxiv-2307-12469.creator: Cen Zhang, Yaowen Zheng, Mingqiang Bai, Yeting Li, Wei Ma, Xiaofei Xie, Yuekang Li, Limin Sun, Yang Liu
arxiv-2307-12469.description: Abstract . † † footnotetext: IIE → \rightarrow Institute of Information Engineering, CAS → \rightarrow Chinese Academy of Sciences. arxiv-2311-11858.title: Theory coherent shrinkage of Time-Varying Parameters in VARs I would like to thank Frank Schorfheide and Andrea Carriero for invaluable guidance and support. I also thank participants at the NBER-NSF SBIES Conference at the Federal Reserve of Philadelphia, the Workshop in Empirical Macroeconomics at
arxiv-2311-11858.creator: Andrea Renzetti
arxiv-2311-11858.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel theory-coherent shrinkage prior for Time-Varying Parameter VARs (TVP-VARs). The prior centers the time-varying parameters on a path implied a priori by an underlying economic theory, chosen to describe the dynamics of the macroeconomic variables in the system.

arxiv-2402-14955.title: Quantile Regression Tree
arxiv-2402-14955.creator: Jaachinma Okafor, Lateefah Isegen, Ark Ifeanyi
arxiv-2402-14955.description: Abstract This study introduces and evaluates the Quantile Regressor Tree (QRT), a novel methodology merging the robust characteristics of quantile regression with the versatility of decision trees. The quantile regressor tree introduces non-linearity to the quantile regression due to the splitting by features in the decision tree, enhancing flexibility while maintaining interpretability.

arxiv-2405-06487.description: Abstract Improving calibration performance in deep learning (DL) classification models is important when planning the use of DL in a decision-support setting. In such a scenario, a confident wrong prediction could lead to a lack of trust and/or harm in a high-risk application.

openalex-w2534848372.creator: Geoff M. Gurr, Anne C. Johnson, Gavin James Ash, Bree A.L. Wilson, Mark M. Ero, C. A. Pilotti, C. F. Dewhurst, Minsheng You
openalex-w2534848372.description: The recent discovery of Bogia coconut syndrome in Papua New Guinea (PNG) is the first report of a lethal yellowing disease (LYD) in Oceania. Numerous outbreaks of LYDs of coconut have been recorded in the Caribbean and Africa since the late Nineteenth century and have caused the

pmc-10550572.title: Federal government tax independence, statutory quota and capital investment
pmc-10550572.creator: Cordelia Onyinyechi Omodero, Philip Olasupo Alege
pmc-10550572.description: The enquiry arose from the necessity for a reevaluation of Nigeria's budgetary system. The current fiscal structure does not appear to be fair enough to foster social development in all of its ramifications. As a result, there is a void in infrastructure development in favor of citizens.

pmc-10631323.title: International Classification of Function, Disability and Health (ICF) Word Mapping to Determine the Human Functioning Associated with Upper Extremity Surgery for Tetraplegia
pmc-10631323.creator: K Anne Sinnott Jerram, Jennifer A Dunn, Richard P Smaill, James W Middleton
pmc-10631323.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Understanding human functioning and disablement, the contributing factors and their interactions in individuals with tetraplegia is important since elective upper extremity (UE) reconstructive surgery is now offered earlier after injury prior to full recognition of what lies ahead. Qualitative and quantitative data were available from a prior series of mixed methods studies, including a case series design capturing the patients’ lived-experience perspectives of nerve or tendon transfer surgery, or not as the case may be.

pmc-10704706.title: “Work with us… to make it more accessible”. What women with intellectual disabilities want from infant-feeding health resources: an exploratory study
pmc-10704706.creator: Emma Douglass, Clare Johnson, Geraldine Lucas, Sally Dowling
pmc-10704706.description: BackgroundMore women with intellectual disabilities are becoming mothers but fewer are known to breastfeed compared with other women. Women with intellectual disabilities are entitled to accessible antenatal and infant feeding information, yet are rarely asked for their views on available resources.

pmc-11535028.title: The role of cydB gene in the biofilm formation by Campylobacter jejuni
pmc-11535028.creator: Jakub Korkus, Patrycja Sałata, Stuart A Thompson, Emil Paluch, Jacek Bania, Ewa Wałecka-Zacharska
pmc-11535028.description: Campylobacter jejuni is a major cause of food- and water-borne bacterial infections in humans. A key factor helping bacteria to survive adverse environmental conditions is biofilm formation ability. Nonetheless, the molecular basis underlying biofilm formation by C. jejuni remains poorly understood. Around thirty genes involved in the regulation and dynamics of C. jejuni biofilm formation have been described so far.

pmc-11548301.title: A Comprehensive Review on the Incremental Sheet Forming of Polycarbonate
pmc-11548301.creator: Antonio Formisano, Massimo Durante
pmc-11548301.description: Incremental sheet forming has emerged as an excellent alternative to other material forming procedures, incrementally deforming flat metal sheets into complex three-dimensional profiles. The main characteristics of this process are its versatility and cost-effectiveness; additionally, it allows for greater formability compared to conventional sheet forming processes. Recently, its application has been extended to polymers and composites.

pmc-11643671.title: The Reversible Electron Transfer Within Stimuli-Responsive Hydrochromic Supramolecular Material Containing Pyridinium Oxime and Hexacyanoferrate (II) Ions
pmc-11643671.creator: Blaženka Foretić, Teodoro Klaser, Juraj Ovčar, Ivor Lončarić, Dijana Žilić, Ana Šantić, Zoran Štefanić, Alen Bjelopetrović, Jasminka Popović, Igor Picek
pmc-11643671.description: The structural and electronic features of the stimuli-responsive supramolecular inter-ionic charge-transfer material containing electron accepting N-benzylyridinium-4-oxime cation (BPA4+) and electron donating hexacyanoferrate (II) are reported. The study of reversible stimuli-induced transformation between hydrated reddish-brown (BPA4)4[Fe(CN)6]·10H2O and anhydrous blue (BPA4)4[Fe(CN)6] revealed the origin of observed hydrochromic behavior.

pmc-11713295.title: AD pathology in LBD – Implications for Clinical Trials
pmc-11713295.creator: Bhavana Patel
pmc-11713295.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a common copathology in Lewy body dementia (LBD). The presence of AD is associated with a distinct clinical presentation, faster progression, and shorter survival in LBD. However, the relationship between‐alpha synuclein and AD remains incompletely understood.

pmc-12524920.title: Cyberchondria and Health Anxiety in Patients Visiting Hematology Outpatient Clinic: Reflection of Digitalisation
pmc-12524920.creator: Kadir Ilkkilic, Recep Evcen
pmc-12524920.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Cyberchondria is characterized by heightened health anxiety resulting from excessive online health information seeking, and studies on this topic in the field of hematology are limited. The aim of this study was to examine the levels of cyberchondria and health anxiety among patients attending the hematology outpatient clinic without a diagnosis of malignancy, and to evaluate the relationship between these two factors.

pmc-12553166.title: Single-cell stemness analysis highlights Midkine-LRP1 pathway and identifies new bladder cancer subtypes
pmc-12553166.creator: Cheng Qian, Jin Qin, Zixian Lin, Shenggan Wang, Anmei Deng, Tengda Li
pmc-12553166.description: Bladder cancer (BC) is among the ten most common malignant tumors worldwide. Tumor stem cells contribute significantly to postoperative recurrence and disease progression. Understanding stem cell interactions with other tissue cells and developing a prognostic model may improve BC management. Through single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified tumor stem cells in BC tissue.

pmc-12642208.title: A novel protocol for protoplast isolation, transfection, and culture in Cannabis sativa L
pmc-12642208.creator: Katarzyna Stelmach-Wityk, Kamil Szymonik, Andrew Maxwell Phineas Jones, Ewa Grzebelus
pmc-12642208.description: BackgroundProtoplasts are a valuable tool for studying gene expression and applying genome editing techniques. Given the high medicinal and industrial potential of Cannabis sativa L., developing an efficient protoplast-to-plant regeneration protocol is highly desirable. Due to its recalcitrant nature, a complete plant regeneration from cannabis protoplasts has not yet been achieved.

pmc-12659521.title: Real-world effectiveness of eptinezumab in chronic migraine—increase in good days in three subgroups: psychiatric comorbidities, prior subcutaneous anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide therapy, and migraine-associated brain fog
pmc-12659521.creator: Charles Argoff, Fawad A Khan, Steven P Herzog, Ryan M Smith, Seema Soni-Brahmbhatt, Divya Asher, Susanne F Awad, S Wald Grossman, Foram Patel, Dawn C Buse
pmc-12659521.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe REVIEW study evaluated the real-world experiences of individuals treated with eptinezumab for chronic migraine (CM) in the outpatient setting. This post hoc analysis explored eptinezumab effectiveness in three participant subgroups: those who had self-reported psychiatric comorbidities, those previously treated with subcutaneous anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide (anti-CGRP) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) for migraine prevention, or those who had reported ever experiencing symptoms of brain fog.MethodsAdults with a CM diagnosis who completed ≥ 2 eptinezumab infusion cycles provided survey responses that included the number of

pmc-13225242.title: Efficacy of Levetiracetam in Patients With Pediatric Epilepsy
pmc-13225242.creator: Simona Balestrini, Donella Puliti, Martina Lombardini, Alessandra Bettiol, Simone Gasparini, Marta Lomonaco, Elena Margherita Presotto, Elena Pia Dalmazio Tarantino, Salvatore De Masi, Renzo Guerrini
pmc-13225242.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and ObjectivesLevetiracetam (LEV) is widely used in pediatric epilepsies because of its favorable pharmacokinetics, ease of administration, and perceived tolerability. However, its comparative efficacy relative to established antiseizure medications (ASMs) in children remains uncertain.

pmc-13256547.title: Adverse Hemodynamics in Acute Heart Failure Patients Are Associated with Skeletal Muscle Stress Biomarkers
pmc-13256547.creator: Kamil A. Kobak, Monika Kasztura, Krystian Josiak, Robert Zymliński, Natalia Świątoniowska-Lonc, Waldemar Banasiak, Kinga Węgrzynowska-Teodorczyk
pmc-13256547.description: Acute heart failure (AHF) causes abrupt hemodynamic disturbances, including reduced forward flow and venous congestion, which may extend beyond the heart and contribute to peripheral organ stress. Skeletal muscle may be particularly vulnerable to these changes, but the relationship between acute hemodynamic status and circulating markers of skeletal muscle stress and regulation remains unclear.

pmc-13386659.title: Ocular Misalignment and Motility Limitation in Orbital Tumors
pmc-13386659.creator: Min Seok Kang, Namju Kim, Hee Kyung Yang, Jeong-Min Hwang, Shweta Negi
pmc-13386659.description: PurposeTo predict prognosis and aid in the treatment of residual strabismus/ocular misalignment by analyzing the pattern of ocular motility disturbances caused by orbital tumors, and investigating factors associated with the severity of misalignment or motility limitation.MethodsThe medical records of 63 patients diagnosed with orbital tumors were retrospectively reviewed. The location, type, and size of the tumor were noted.

pmc-13425961.title: Predictive value of a combined nomogram model integrating ultrasound and cytology for 2025 ATA risk stratification of lymph node negative papillary thyroid carcinoma
pmc-13425961.creator: Xiachuan Qin, Xiaoling Liu, Fanding He, Weihan Xiao, Xianjun Ye
pmc-13425961.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThis study aimed to predict the 2025 American Thyroid Association (ATA) risk stratification of lymph node negative (N0) papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) patients using preoperative ultrasonic and cytological features to provide guidance for clinical treatment strategies.MethodsIn this multicenter, retrospective study, 500 N0 PTC patients who underwent total thyroidectomy with lymph node dissection were included across 2 institutions from September 2018 to February 2024. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate-high recurrence risk groups based on the 2025 ATA risk stratification system.

pmc-13563050.title: TTP‐Like Syndrome and Subsequent Non‐Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in HbSC Disease: A Case Report
pmc-13563050.creator: Benjamin Vieten, Jan Vorwerk, Jan Morf, Alice Dauth, Stefan Sondermann, Peter Schramm, Tobias Graf, Nikolas von Bubnoff, Lorenz Oelschläger, Cyrus Khandanpour
pmc-13563050.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sickle cell disease (SCD) with hemoglobin‐ (Hb‐) SC genotype is often considered a milder SCD variant, yet life‐threatening complications can occur. A 26‐year‐old man with HbSC disease presented with an infection triggered vaso‐occlusive crisis (VOC), acute chest syndrome (ACS), severe thrombocytopenia, Coombs‐negative hemolysis with schistocytes, acute kidney injury, and markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in the setting of Klebsiella pneumoniae sepsis. The resulting severe thrombotic microangiopathy‐ (TMA‐) like phenotype initially raised concern for thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP).

pmc-13668692.title: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-13668692.creator: Tina Cascone, Mark M Awad, Jonathan D Spicer, Jie He, Shun Lu, Fumihiro Tanaka, Robin Cornelissen, Lubos B Petruzelka, Yang Gao, Jean-Louis Pujol, Hiroyuki Ito, Ludmila de Oliveira Muniz Koch, Tudor-Eliade Ciuleanu, Lin Wu, Sabine Bohnet, Yasutaka Watanabe, Janis M Taube, Julie Stein Deutsch, Cinthy
pmc-13668692.description: Perioperative nivolumab significantly improved event-free survival (EFS) compared with placebo in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the CheckMate 77T study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04025879)1. Here, after randomization, 98 out of 229 patients who received nivolumab and 92 out of 232 patients who received placebo had evaluable biomarkers (41% of randomized patients).
